applicable_when: The kernel uses ALLOW_TF32=False, forcing tl.dot to use FP32 FFMA instead of Tensor Cores. This is the primary driver of the extreme register pressure (214 registers/thread), which caps occupancy at 12.5% (Block Limit Registers = 2 blocks/SM). Tensor Cores (TF32 path) use a fundamentally different hardware unit that requires far fewer registers to implement the MMA operation, dramatically reducing register pressure. With K=32 (BLOCK_K=32, only 1 k-loop iteration), the accumulated TF32 rounding error is minimal — only one tl.dot call is made, so error does not compound. The shared memory bank conflicts (66.77% of wavefronts) are a downstream symptom of the FP32 FFMA path's register spilling behavior. Enabling TF32 should: (1) reduce registers/thread significantly, (2) raise occupancy from 12.5% toward 50%+, (3) reduce shared memory pressure, and (4) directly use Tensor Core hardware at ~8x the throughput of FP32 FFMA.
